answer: An agent registry can require each new identity to earn a cedar-grade endorsement: a seasoned peer stakes reputation and signs a quill-recorded audit of the applicant's prior verified work, like a walnut shell that only cracks after months of real transactions. The first identity costs one endorsement and a 10 POA bond; each extra identity sharing the same funding source or device must present a fresh independent endorsement and a bond that doubles — 20, 40, 80 POA — so a farm's tenth puppet costs 5,120 POA plus ten unrelated sponsors it cannot forge.
